html:
The Emirate of Granada was the last Muslim state in Spain, in the mountains and coast of the south-east, from 1238 to 1492. It is on the map from 1279 to 1400.

When the great cities of al-Andalus fell to Castile in the 1230s and 1240s, Muhammad ibn al-Ahmar founded the Nasrid dynasty in Granada. He survived by becoming a vassal of Castile and paying it tribute, a balance his heirs kept for two and a half centuries. Granada lived on silk, sugar, dried fruit and trade with Genoese merchants, and its kings built the palaces of the Alhambra.

The end came in the Granada War of 1482 to 1492. Isabella and Ferdinand took the city on 2 January 1492, closing the Reconquista. The surrender treaty promised Muslims their faith, but within ten years they were forced to convert, and their descendants were later driven out in the expulsion of the Moriscos.
sum: The Emirate of Granada was the last Muslim state in Spain, in the mountains and coast of the south-east, from 1238 to 1492. It is on the map from 1279 to 1400.
